endorsements.quote: As good practice, prior written informed consent should be obtained before using any type of AI scribe.

Thus, physicians need to be clear that they should not send PHI through these services, because ChatGPT (and others) essentially retain their input to train, and it may potentially be possible to reidentify and expose the incorporated PHI.
However, careful proofreading of the AI-generated language by the physician signing the note is essential.

We recommend medical AI developers incorporate better ways (eg, highlighted text, confidence scores expressed in percentages) to draw physicians’ attention to where the AI has low confidence and prompt the user and/or proofreader to pay attention and issue confirmation or corrections.

unlisted_practices: AI scribe developers should incorporate an introductory phase in which the AI learns the distinct voices of the physician and office staff.
AI scribe developers should alert the physician when a new voice enters the encounter so the physician can confirm the encounter is continuing or end the visit.
Medical AI developers should consider ways to achieve more uniform AI scribe outputs across similar inputs.
Medical AI developers should incorporate an introductory phase to learn the user's dictation style and compliance prerequisites, and use physician manual edits as feedback.
Medical AI developers should allow retraining or overriding of brand-name vernacular, for example through third-party plug-ins, to reduce hallucinated substitutions.
Physicians should adopt a signature disclaimer stating that a note was drafted using AI and may contain errors of omission, substitution, or fabrication.
Physicians should not become complacent about proofreading AI-generated notes as the technology improves.
Medical AI developers should use robust regulatory oversight to protect data privacy and security, adhere to ethical guidelines, and de-bias their algorithms.
AI scribe companies should consider disclosure requirements in different jurisdictions.
Medical AI developers should test for accuracy and detect and correct deviations from intended output.
Physicians should consider dictating procedure notes separately or using templates rather than relying on AI scribes.
